title: McDonald's earlier career and recordings
summary: Jones recalls McDonald's New York dates, his years on the road with a flower company, and the band's fame, but is unsure about their recordings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did McDonald go on the road before this time? Had he been on the road?
Yeah, he'd been to New York, played the Hippodrome Theater, several games in New York for Charles Dillian Yes, I remember that name.
Yeah, he was. How long had McDonald been in the music business before 1920?
Oh, I guess he'd been in the music business eight or nine years before I ever met him. He played around that road for years with the Ballast Flower Company. Ballast Flower.
Now, the Flower Company had some radio programs, too. Is that where you...
That's the same. He was on that program.
Well, that started after 1920, I think. Now, did he work too far before?
He started before then. Is that so? Yeah, he was working there when I joined him, when he got this and gave him to come to Chicago in 1920.
Do you remember that McDonald did other recording, did recording work?
There are some records in the name of Louisville Jug Band, but I think that's Clifford Hayes' group.
I don't know. I wouldn't say because I don't know, but I do know he made a record, made some records. I don't know. They were famous when I started working with them. They were famous.
